blogTitle: Solving focal point issues with the right Sitting room art
videoTitle: Solving focal point issues with the right Sitting room art
script:
Solving focal point issues with the right Sitting room art

You know that feeling when you walk into your sitting room and something just feels… off? [warmly] Chances are, it's your focal point — and the right wall art can fix it.

Here's the thing — well-chosen sitting room art can instantly establish a mood, guide the eye, and bring real HARMONY to a space.

Okay — quick key takeaways before we dig in: size, colour, placement, and layering ALL matter when you're solving focal point problems with art.

Some sitting rooms just feel… unsettled, right? When no single element draws the eye, the whole space lacks harmony — and that's your focal point challenge.

It often comes from walls that are bare or overcrowded, or furniture that just doesn't frame ANYTHING — so the eye wanders with no place to land.

A really common one — the fireplace, the telly, AND the sofa wall all competing for attention at once… honestly, it leaves guests visually disoriented.

[curious] Here's where colour and style really come into play — bold furniture patterns can accidentally OVERSHADOW your wall art before it even gets a chance.

I once helped a client whose red sofa was totally drowning out a beautiful landscape painting — swapping it to soft creams made the art click in the whole room.

Think of your wall art as a VISUAL anchor — the right piece guides attention, balances awkward layouts, and invites those lovely lingering moments of calm.

Abstract pieces with bold strokes energise minimalist rooms… serene landscapes bring tranquillity to busier spaces — it's about matching the ART style to the room's energy.

And this set — honestly, one of my favourites — three Japanese-inspired prints that bring such a calm, collected feel to any sitting room wall.

Scale is everything — an OVERSIZED piece can overwhelm, and one that's too small just gets lost on the wall… you want something that feels intentional.

A little tip I love: hang art so the centre of the piece sits roughly at EYE level — about 145 to 150 centimetres from the floor. It just feels right.

For placement — above a sofa, keep about 15 to 20 centimetres of gap between the top of the sofa and the BOTTOM of the frame… trust me, it makes a huge difference.

These Japanese flower prints are gorgeous for this — soft, layered, and they sit beautifully above a sofa or console without overwhelming the space at all.

Art doesn't live in isolation — it should TALK to your cushions, throws, rugs, and other decorative touches to create real cohesion across the whole room.

Layering different textures and tones — like pairing a graphic print with softer natural elements — adds real DEPTH and makes the room feel more inviting.

[excited] Real transformations — I've seen rooms go from feeling completely muddled to having this instant sense of calm and purpose, just by adding the RIGHT piece of art.

A deep navy sofa, for instance — pair it with wall art in soft pastels or metallic accents, and suddenly it catches the light and adds DIMENSION without overpowering anything.

And for coastal or nature-inspired spaces… [softly] something like this coastline set just breathes life into the room — calm, airy, effortless.

The big lesson from all of this — don't hang art as an afterthought… treat it as the STARTING point, and let it guide everything else in the room around it.

To sum it all up — identify your focal point challenge, choose art that anchors it, get the scale and placement RIGHT, and let the colours do the talking.

Pro tip — if you're unsure where to start, just pick ONE wall, choose a piece that speaks to you, and build the room's palette and texture outward from THERE.

And if you want more inspiration — there's a full guide to living room ideas over on the site, covering everything from colour psychology to gallery wall layouts… well worth a look.

From colour theory and design principles to gallery wall layouts and art sizing. Download them all from our site!

Find all you need to transform your home into a calming oasis!

Happy Decorating!
